REST CRUD controller with validation (@Valid and DTO records)

When validation fails, @Valid throws MethodArgumentNotValidException, which becomes a 400 response. Records make good immutable DTOs. Return 201 with a Location header for creates and 204 for deletes. This needs spring-boot-starter-validation.
Global exception handler (@RestControllerAdvice and ProblemDetail)

ProblemDetail (new in Spring 6) produces RFC 7807 application/problem+json bodies. You can also extend ResponseEntityExceptionHandler or set spring.mvc.problemdetails.enabled=true to get the built-in handlers.
Pagination and sorting endpoint

Spring resolves Pageable from the page, size and sort parameters. Cap the page size with spring.data.web.pageable.max-page-size. Return a Slice when you don't need the total count, which skips the COUNT query.
Service layer with @Transactional

By default, a rollback happens only for unchecked exceptions. Use rollbackFor = Exception.class to include checked ones. A self-call such as this.transfer() skips the proxy, so @Transactional has no effect on it. readOnly = true lets Hibernate skip dirty checking.
Custom validator annotation
The message, groups and payload attributes are required. Validators are Spring beans, so you can inject a repository into one, for example to check for a unique email.
File upload endpoint (multipart)

Check that the file isn't empty, check its type and size, and never trust the client's file name. Uploads over the limit throw MaxUploadSizeExceededException, which you can handle in the advice class. In production, stream the file to object storage such as S3.
Calling another service with RestClient (and WebClient)

RestClient (Spring 6.1, Boot 3.2+) is the modern blocking client and replaces RestTemplate. Use WebClient in reactive apps. Set timeouts, and add retries or a circuit breaker with Resilience4j. An @HttpExchange interface is the declarative option.
JWT filter with a Spring Security 6 SecurityFilterChain

Spring Security 6 removed WebSecurityConfigurerAdapter, so you declare a SecurityFilterChain bean using the lambda DSL. authorizeRequests and antMatchers were replaced by authorizeHttpRequests and requestMatchers. If you don't need a hand-written filter, oauth2ResourceServer(o -> o.jwt(...)) handles validation for you.
Scheduled job with @Scheduled

A Spring cron expression has 6 fields: second, minute, hour, day, month and weekday. fixedRate counts from the start of each run, while fixedDelay counts from the end of the previous one. With several instances running, add ShedLock so only one of them runs the job. The default scheduler uses a single thread.
Controller unit test with @WebMvcTest and MockMvc

@WebMvcTest starts only the web layer (controllers, advice and filters), so it runs fast, and the service is mocked. If Spring Security is on the classpath, add @WithMockUser or import your security config. Use @SpringBootTest with Testcontainers for full integration tests.
Type-safe configuration with @ConfigurationProperties (record + validation)

Prefer @ConfigurationProperties over many @Value fields: it groups settings, supports relaxed binding (base-url to baseUrl), converts types such as Duration and DataSize, and with @Validated the app fails at startup on a bad value instead of at runtime. Records give immutable, constructor-bound properties. Override per environment with profiles (application-prod.yml) or environment variables (APP_PAYMENT_BASEURL).
Caching with @Cacheable, @CachePut and @CacheEvict

Caching works through a proxy, so calling a @Cacheable method from another method in the same class bypasses the cache (the same self-invocation trap as @Transactional). Cache DTOs, not JPA entities. With several app instances use a shared cache such as Redis, otherwise each instance has its own stale copy. Always set a TTL and a size limit.
@Async with a custom executor, returning CompletableFuture

@Async methods must be public and called from another bean (proxy again). Return void or CompletableFuture. Exceptions from void methods don't reach the caller, so configure an AsyncUncaughtExceptionHandler. The async method runs in a different thread, so it does not share the caller's transaction or security context unless you propagate them. For real reliability (retries, surviving restarts) use a message queue instead.
Publish a domain event and handle it after commit (@TransactionalEventListener)

Events decouple the order logic from side effects (email, audit, analytics). A plain @EventListener runs immediately and synchronously, inside the transaction; @TransactionalEventListener(AFTER_COMMIT) waits for a successful commit, so you never email about an order that was rolled back. For cross-service events that must not be lost, use the transactional outbox pattern (write the event to a table in the same transaction, then publish it to Kafka or RabbitMQ).
Unit test a service with Mockito (no Spring context)

Plain Mockito tests start in milliseconds because no Spring context loads; use them for business logic. @Mock creates a fake, @InjectMocks builds the class under test with those fakes (constructor injection), ArgumentCaptor checks what was passed, and verify(..., never()) asserts something did not happen. Follow Arrange–Act–Assert and test one behaviour per test.
Integration test with @SpringBootTest and Testcontainers (real MySQL)

Testcontainers starts a real database in Docker, so you test the actual SQL, constraints and Flyway/Liquibase migrations instead of an H2 approximation. @ServiceConnection removes the need for @DynamicPropertySource. Keep these tests fewer than unit tests (test pyramid), and reuse one container across tests through a shared base class to keep the suite fast.
Request logging filter with a correlation id (MDC)

Every log line written while handling the request now carries the same id, so you can trace one request across services when the id is forwarded in outgoing calls. A servlet filter sees every request (including static and error paths) and can wrap the request or response; a Spring MVC HandlerInterceptor runs only around controller handlers and knows which handler was chosen. In production, Micrometer Tracing adds trace and span ids automatically.
CORS for an Angular front end (Spring Security 6)

CORS is enforced by the browser: before a cross-origin request with custom headers, it sends a preflight OPTIONS request, and the server must answer with the allowed origin, methods and headers. With Spring Security, configure CORS in the security chain, otherwise the preflight is rejected as unauthenticated before your @CrossOrigin or WebMvcConfigurer settings are reached. You cannot combine allowCredentials(true) with the wildcard origin *. In development, the Angular dev-server proxy (proxy.conf.json) avoids CORS entirely.
